original_query: select c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice, sum(l_quantity) from customer, orders, lineitem where o_orderkey in ( select l_orderkey from lineitem group by l_orderkey having sum(l_quantity) > 315 ) and c_custkey = o_custkey and o_orderkey = l_orderkey group by c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice order by o_totalprice desc, o_orderdate limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH order_qty AS (
    SELECT l_orderkey, SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_qty
    FROM lineitem
    GROUP BY l_orderkey
    HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 315
)
SELECT c.c_name, c.c_custkey, o.o_orderkey, o.o_orderdate, o.o_totalprice, oq.sum_qty
FROM order_qty oq
JOIN orders o ON o.o_orderkey = oq.l_orderkey
JOIN customer c ON c.c_custkey = o.o_custkey
ORDER BY o.o_totalprice DESC, o.o_orderdate
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The IN subquery scans lineitem (60M rows) to find qualifying orderkeys, while the outer query scans lineitem again and re-aggregates the same SUM(l_quantity). Replace the IN with a JOIN against a CTE that aggregates lineitem once and reuses sum_qty for both the filter (HAVING) and the output, eliminating the duplicate lineitem scan.

Remove the outer GROUP BY and SUM aggregation: since order_qty yields one row per orderkey, orders.o_orderkey and customer.c_custkey are unique, the original GROUP BY is a no-op for uniqueness and the outer sum(l_quantity) equals the CTE's sum_qty.

Join the filtered CTE (small result: only orders with quantity > 315) to orders and customer via primary keys, replacing the original three-way cartesian-style WHERE join with explicit inner joins, enabling efficient hash/nested-loop joins.
The HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 315 filter is applied inside the CTE immediately after aggregation, ensuring only qualifying orders flow into the joins, reducing the join and sort input cardinality.
